Success through effort and determination
Examination Results
Sixth Form

Our Ethos
OUR SCHOOL MOTTO
“SUCCESS THROUGH EFFORT AND DETERMINATION”
At Brampton Manor Academy, we passionately believe that all students can be successful if they show real effort and determination to do their best. We know that this is true and can point to the success of thousands of former and current students to prove the point.
We celebrate success and applaud effort and determination whenever our students really go ‘the extra mile’ to be the best that they can be. This may be shown in lessons, in clubs, through homework, through helping others or through any contribution to the rich life of our school or the local community.
Rewarding effort and determination is at the heart of our philosophy as a school. We have many academically able students in our school, but our system encourages students of all abilities to be outstanding. That’s one of the reasons why our students make outstanding progress in their learning.
OUR SCHOOL MISSION STATEMENT
The values which underpin everything we do are expressed in our Mission Statement:
THE BRAMPTON SKILLSET
We recognise that a top quality education consists of much more than just academic qualifications. The skills and qualities which we instil in our young people will have a profound impact on the quality of their lives and their future opportunities. Their personal and social strengths will be integral to everything they achieve. At Brampton Manor we work hard to develop students who are:
Resilient

About Us
Brampton Manor Academy is one of the top performing academic sixth forms in the country. Offering outstanding A Level teaching, we have exceptionally high standards with an established tradition of academic achievement. Our fantastic reputation is supported by a stunning track record of success. The latest performance tables published by the Department for Education in 2025 confirm Brampton Manor delivered some of the best A Level results in the country, as we have done consistently since our Sixth Form opened in 2012. We have an unrivalled progression rate to the elite Russell Group of universities, including Oxbridge and medical school, which has placed us in the top few schools in the UK several years running. In 2024 alone we sent 56 students to Oxford and Cambridge, over 350 students have progressed to Oxbridge in the last 7 years, an achievement that captured the attention of the world’s media.
This level of success is a tribute to the commitment, dedication and hard work of our students and is underpinned by many elements, including exceptional teaching, a diverse programme of enrichment, envious facilities, a first-rate university preparation programme and an ethos and culture which supports and guides all our students in ensuring their time at Brampton is an amazing one.
As a Sixth Form we believe that there is no limit to what our students can achieve. In fact, we are constantly challenging our students to aim higher than they ever have before. We also want our students to enjoy their Sixth Form experience and provide plenty of social, sporting, artistic and recreational activities to help ensure a healthy work / life balance.
We are incredibly proud of what our outstanding students have achieved to date but, as a Sixth Form whose results and university progression has improved every year since we opened, are even more excited by what lies ahead.
We encourage talented Year 11 students who share our ambition and appetite for hard work to consider making an application to study in our Sixth Form so that you can become part of the next chapter of this success story.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brampton Manor Academy - Welcome from the Executive Principal
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Executive Principal
Welcome to our website and thank you for taking the time to learn more about our school. We are a vibrant and high-achieving 11–18 school proudly serving the Newham community. Our students come from a wide range of backgrounds and abilities, and this diversity gives our school its energy, character, and strength.
Our success is rooted in an unwavering focus on what matters most: exceptional teaching, meaningful learning, and high expectations for every student. Students benefit from inspiring teaching, positive behaviour for learning and strong, purposeful leadership. While we are proud of what we have achieved, we are never complacent and are always seeking to improve further.
Students make excellent progress because they experience a rich and ambitious curriculum, alongside outstanding care, guidance, and support. Our motto, “success through effort and determination” underpins daily life at the academy and reflects our clear mission: to ensure that no child is left behind.
We offer a broad blend of academic and vocational pathways, supported by outstanding facilities. These include a state-of-the-art theatre, audio-visual recording studios, excellent sports and fitness provision, and modern, well-resourced classrooms, workshops, and laboratories. High-quality IT and related technology supports learning across all areas of the school.
We hope this website gives you a clear sense of who we are and what we stand for. If you would like to find out more or have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us at info@bramptonmanor.org.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brampton Manor Academy - Careers in the Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Careers in the Curriculum
Brampton Manor Academy is committed to developing the life chances of all students and aims to encourage and inspire pupils through a comprehensive programme of CEIAG. Employability is not just an add-on but a golden thread, weaved throughout the school's leadership and governance, curriculum and careers events.
The school has a careers co-ordinator running a wide variety of events as part of our careers programme for all year groups. As well as discussions and activities forming part of the curriculum and posters in individual departments, there is also help and advice via our independent careers advisor rom 15billion, access to online careers package (Kudos), careers assemblies, registration activities and lots more.
At KS3 (Year 7, 8 and 9)
Students participate in a range of activities which includes learning about themselves; their personality, strengths and qualities. They will begin to explore different career options in the modern world and gain an awareness of how they begin to research and plan various career paths. Year 9 pupils will focus on KS4 options and making appropriate subject choices for their chosen career pathway. All year groups will meet with employers and other outside agencies to gain independent and impartial advice about the options which are best suited to them as individuals.
At KS4 (Year 10 and 11)
Year 10 students are given the opportunity to undertake work experience, as well as taking part in a careers event (Boss Day) which will develop their employability skills. Year 11's are offered an individual and / or group session with the independent Careers Advisor and will also focus on their post-16 options, while learning how to make effective transition from KS4. They also have the opportunity to attend the Careers Fair at Excel Arena where there are potential employers from different sectors as well as college and apprenticeship providers. Both year groups will have a range of events and opportunities to gain independent and impartial advice about options which is best suited to them as individuals.
At KS5 (Year 12 and 13)
Both years will have access to a number of employer led careers events such as Careers Fair in the Excel Arena. Also important to KS5 is the opportunity to the following:-
LSE - STEM subject awareness

pageCache.pageTitle: Brampton Manor Academy - Board of Directors
pageCache.text:
Board of Directors
Marion Faust, MBE (Chair)
As Governor and later Chair of Governors at Brampton Manor School (and now Chair of the Board of Directors of Brampton Manor Trust), Marion’s total and unwavering commitment to the school spans almost three decades! Her children attended the school and since then, Marion has given of her time very generously and has been a strong advocate for the young people. She believes firmly that all children can achieve regardless of their socio-economic background. As a result, she has presided over our rapid and sustained improvement, making us the best school in Newham and one of the highest performing schools in the country. Marion has been at the forefront of championing and helping to foster links between business and education in Newham for over two decades. She is an ardent believer in the role that businesses can play in the wider curriculum and in helping young people to gain worthwhile life and employability skills. In this regard, she has helped to recruit leaders of successful businesses to join the governing bodies of local skills, provide work experience/placements for young people and to ensure that the in the rapidly growing finance and business economy in East London, local children and young people are well positioned to secure those jobs.
IAN PORTER (Chair of Resources & Audit Committee)
Ian Porter is a qualified Chartered Accountant and is currently the chief executive of 15billion-ebp, an organisation involved in delivering quality work and career related programmes for schools, employers and young people. Ian brings with him, a considerable wealth of experience in the public and private sectors and joined the board of Brampton Manor Trust in January 2017.
CHIRAG PATEL (Director)
Chirag joined the Trust’s Board of Directors, bringing a wealth of experience of more than two decades within the banking sector. Chirag is currently a Managing Director at HSBC Group, co-running the Global Foreign Exchange and Precious Metals Derivatives Trading business.
JULIAN TAYLOR (Director)
Julian is the Senior Partner (or Chair) at Simmons & Simmons, an international law firm. He continues to practise as an employment lawyer. He is also a co-founder and trustee of the Pennies scheme, the digital charity box. Julian has previously been a governor of a primary school, a trustee of a youth volunteering charity and, much earlier in his career, a teacher.
MATILDE VAQUERA-MOSQUERO (Director)
Maty is a modern foreign languages teacher with over 30 years teaching experience. She started her teaching career at Brentwood County High school from where she joined Seven Kings High School initially as Deputy Head of Languages/Head of Spanish and later as Head of Languages. She subsequently joined Little Ilford School as Head of Languages; joined the extended SLT as an Associate Assistant Headteacher and latterly as an Advanced Skills Teacher for Assessment for Learning. In this capacity, Maty supported various schools within the borough with improving pedagogy and pupil outcomes in languages and other subject areas. Maty is currently a substantive member of the SLT as an assistant headteacher and plays a crucial role in helping to provide strategic leadership, including budgeting/financial management of the various areas that she is accountable for. Maty is a great believer in comprehensive education and a strong advocate for disadvantaged pupils. She has an impressive and proven track record of public examination success and will undoubtedly be a welcome addition to the board.
DENNIS HULL (Director)
Dennis is an energetic IT transformation leader who is passionate about delivering continuous improvement and benefits. Proven experience working in the Telecommunication industry creating multi-million pounds of benefits across AR/AI, Cloud Services, Data, Fibre broadband, Optical Services, IOT, Network Intelligence, Voice, Mobile and UK Regulatory projects and programmes.
Dennis understands that children are the next generation of societies professionals, role models and leaders and is enthused to share his experience to shape the future.
PETER WHITTLE (Director)
Peter Whittle is a vastly experienced school teacher and leader with over 40 years of experience working in Newham schools. He was previously Principal of Langdon Academy and latterly worked as an Associate Principal for the Trust. Peter is passionate about the transformative power of education and is a strong advocate for promoting equality of opportunity for all students.
Dr Dayo Olukoshi, OBE (Executive Principal)
Dr Olukoshi was the headteacher of Brampton Manor School until April 2011, when it converted to Academy status and was appointed the Principal of Brampton Manor Academy. The school has enjoyed tremendous growth and success under his leadership and in 2012 and 2018, Ofsted rated the school as outstanding in all categories. Brampton Manor Academy was invited by the DfE to sponsor another local school, (Langdon School) and in January 2014, Brampton Manor multi-academy trust was formed, with Langdon Academy as an integral member of the family. In the 2015 Queen’s Birthday Honours, Dr Olukoshi was awarded an OBE for services to Education.
